commands.name: cross001_first_time_journey
commands.command: reset isolated MLX_STACK_HOME -> mlx-stack init --accept-defaults -> pull each stack model -> mlx-stack up -> curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/models -> mlx-stack down -> verify no pid files and ports closed

commands.name: cross007_config_propagation
commands.command: config set litellm-port 5000; init; pull all; up; curl :5000; down; set memory-budget-pct 60; recommend/init; set default-quant int8; pull without --quant; set model-dir custom; pull/models validation

commands.name: cross012_saved_benchmark_override
commands.command: write unknown profile m9-max-128 (bandwidth 404) -> recommend --show-all (baseline estimated 77.0 for qwen3.5-8b) -> bench qwen3.5-8b --save -> recommend --show-all

commands.name: cross013_data_consistency
commands.command: profile -> recommend -> init -> bench; pull updates models.json and models output; tamper schema_version to 999 then up (expect reject); init --force; up --dry-run and verify vllm_flags translation

assertionResults.reason: In a clean isolated home, init generated stack/litellm config, all three configured tier models were pulled, up reported healthy services including LiteLLM on port 4000, /v1/models returned HTTP 200 with tier IDs (standard/fast/longctx), and down left no PID files with ports 4000/8000/8001/8002 closed.

Propagation checks passed for memory-budget-pct (recommend/init budget 76.8 GB), default-quant (pull without --quant used int8), and model-dir (pull/models used custom directory). The exact litellm-port 5000 startup requirement was blocked by an external host-level port conflict (up reported 'Port 5000 already in use by PID 0 (<unknown>)' and curl to :5000 returned 403 from non-mlx-stack service). Workaround validation with port 5001 confirmed up starts LiteLLM on configured non-default port.

With unknown profile m9-max-128 (bandwidth 404), recommend --show-all initially showed qwen3.5-8b at 77.0 tok/s (est.). After bench qwen3.5-8b --save, saved benchmark recorded gen_tps=84.7386 and subsequent recommend used 84.7 tok/s for qwen3.5-8b without '(est.)', demonstrating saved benchmark override and estimated-label removal for the saved model.

profile wrote profile.json (m5-max-128) and downstream recommend/init/bench consumed it successfully; pull created models.json entry that matched models CLI output; up rejected unsupported schema_version=999 with exit code 1; and all tier vllm_flags from stack YAML appeared in up --dry-run command lines.

frictions.description: litellm pinned-version mismatch warning (`installed v1.82.6, expected v1.67.2`) appears in up output and adds noise during flow checks.
frictions.resolution: Treated as non-blocking for behavior validation; startup and assertions proceeded normally.

blockers.description: Host port 5000 is already occupied by a non-mlx-stack process in this environment, preventing direct validation that `litellm-port 5000` can actually bind and serve.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Confirmed config propagation to up (skipped with explicit port-5000 conflict message), then validated same behavior on nearby free port 5001 where up started LiteLLM and /v1/models returned 200.

summary: Tested 4 assigned misc cross assertions in isolated CLI mode: 3 passed (VAL-CROSS-001, VAL-CROSS-012, VAL-CROSS-013), 0 failed, 1 blocked (VAL-CROSS-007 blocked by external port-5000 conflict despite successful propagation checks for other config fields).
